name: Zapier
tagline: The largest catalog of ready-made integrations on the market
description: Connects thousands of SaaS apps with no code, with built-in AI actions and a history of every task; the fastest on-ramp to automation for small teams.
priceNote: Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Anyone who needs to automate a SaaS process in an afternoon, with no technical team
pros: Catalog with thousands of apps and the shortest time to a first working automation
Each app ships with actions, fields and authentication already solved, so you never guess at an API
The platform's AI agents summarize and classify data inside the Zap itself
Run history, task replay and community templates ready to adapt
cons: Task billing gets expensive fast: a five-step automation is five tasks per round
There is no self-hosted version, which rules out keeping sensitive data on your own infrastructure
Runs with many steps are slower than alternatives such as n8n or Make
Support and learning material are almost entirely in English

features.name: App catalog
features.detail: Ready connectors for CRM, email, spreadsheets, ERP and social media

features.name: Native AI actions
features.detail: Extract, classify and summarize text inside the flow, without calling an API

features.name: Zaps and tables
features.detail: Intermediate table to process batches of data on each run

features.name: Supervised agents
features.detail: Agents take actions and request human approval before sending

features.name: Monitor and history
features.detail: Run dashboard, failed tasks and batch reprocessing

useCases: Create the CRM contact and post to Slack when a lead fills in the website form
Generate an executive summary of the sales report every Monday and send it by email
Alert the support team when a customer leaves a bad Google review
Sync the online store inventory with the warehouse sheet without typing anything
bestForWho: Teams starting to automate now that need a working result within a few hours, with no technical budget and no infrastructure of their own.
verdict: Zapier delivers the fastest automation to get live, and that matters more than it looks when nobody in the company can code. The problem shows up on the invoice: every step of the flow counts as a task, so a ten-step scenario running a thousand times a month hits the Professional limit faster than you would expect. Reliability at scale is the other point, because long runs get slow and the paid plan only solves part of that at the top tier. For a small company, the Professional plan with its task limit is enough if you monitor consumption and use error replay. For a mid-sized or large company, compare with Make and n8n before signing, because the cost per active automation almost always ends up higher here.
